destination.name: Glen Innes
destination.tagline: A tablelands town on the New England Highway with a Celtic stone monument and waterfall country nearby.
destination.description: Glen Innes is a town of 6,219 people (2021 census) at 1,062 m on the Northern Tablelands, where the New England and Gwydir highways meet. The Ngarabal name for the site, Gindaaydjin, means plenty of big round stones on the clear plains. Visitors stop for the Australian Standing Stones in Centennial Parklands, Martins Lookout above town and Kings Plains National Park to the north-west.
whyVisit: Walk among the Australian Standing Stones
Walk to Kings Plains Falls after rain

goodToKnow.title: Stones brochure
goodToKnow.detail: The stones are off the Gwydir Highway on Watsons Drive; a brochure explaining them is available from the visitor centre (Monday to Friday 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM).

goodToKnow.title: Falls need rain
goodToKnow.detail: Kings Plains Falls flow only after rain, and the walk is a 3 km return from a site about 50 km from town.

goodToKnow.title: Wikivoyage lists parks further out
goodToKnow.detail: Gibraltar Range and Washpool national parks are 60 to 80 km north-east, so allow a day.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months}: at 1,062 m the town has mild summers, and Wikivoyage's tablelands notes rate summer the pleasantest season.

picks.header_note: Standing Stones (2100 px) is a monument, Kings Plains is another place; neither shows the town in its landscape.
picks.why_note: Only Standing Stones and Kings Plains have Commons photos >=1280. Reason 3 (fossicking) needs a photo.
